result.title: Audit Where Hacks Pay: Budgeted Strong-Verifier Audits Against Reward Hacking in GRPO
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains on cheap checks, such as unit tests, that a policy can learn to game, while a stronger check is too expensive to run on every rollout. We study how to spend a limited strong-verifier budget in GRPO, separating which weakly passing rollouts to audit from what reward a caught hack receives. At a fixed policy state with centered advantages, the expected update depends on a design only through each rollout's marginal audit probability and correction; reflecting a caught hack's reward about the failure reward negates the advantages of an all-hack group; and auditing whole groups with the fewest weak passes first (low-pass budgeted audits, LB) minimizes the advantage mass left on hacks among pass-count designs with a fixed correction when a label's value falls with the pass count. We tested this analysis in actual LLM training: from each run's starting state, the sign of this mass on a frozen panel predicted whether hacking would be suppressed in 33 of 39 runs, including 13 of 16 preregistered ones. In LeetCode (Wong et al., 2026) and Countdown-Code (Khalifa et al., 2026), LB drives hacking to near zero, while random audits with the same penalty and budget do not and use more labels. We also find that the randomness of the update affects training: in Countdown-Code, two unbiased corrections, per-item reward-level IPW and a group-level advantage correction, bring hacking down too but end 6.1-11.8 and 8.0-11.5 points lower in held-out accuracy than LB at the same budget. A full audit, which the group-level correction reproduces in expectation, stays within about two points of LB in three seeds, while LB uses 28% of its labels, and allocating the same correction by pass count recovers most of the loss (one seed). Training outcomes thus depend not only on the expected update but also on the randomness of its estimate.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 GRPO 中强验证器预算有限时如何抑制 reward hacking，把「审计哪些弱通过的 rollout」与「查出的 hack 给什么奖励」拆开分析，提出按组、优先审计弱通过最少的低通过数预算审计（LB），并在 LeetCode 与 Countdown-Code 上显示 LB 能把 hacking 压到近零，且指出更新估计的随机性本身影响最终性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有限验证预算下挑选待核查样本、修正奖励、并考虑估计方差」的设计，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、贡献分配与验证开销权衡提供可核查的方法线索；但论文面向纯文本 RL 训练，与视觉或多模态推理无直接联系。
